title: Slow-cooker baked beans
subtitle: Proper homemade beans in a sweet tomato sauce
excerpt: Haricot beans cooked low and slow in a tomato, mustard, and Worcestershire sauce. Much better than tinned, and very simple to make from scratch.
sourceNotes: Baked beans in tomato sauce are an American dish adopted into British everyday eating through commercial tinned products from the early 20th century. Homemade versions have been popular since the 1970s. This recipe uses tinned haricot beans to avoid overnight soaking.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in portions for up to 3 months. Reheat on the hob with a splash of water.
recipe.batchNotes: Excellent batch recipe. Keeps in the fridge for 5 days and is very versatile.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make a day or two ahead. The sauce thickens and deepens in the fridge.

content.text: Tinned haricot beans work well here and save the overnight soak needed for dried beans. The beans cook in the sauce from the start and absorb it throughout the day. By the time the lid comes off, the sauce will have thickened around the beans and they will be soft and well seasoned all the way through.

The dark brown sugar and Worcestershire sauce are what separate this from a plain tomato sauce. Use both; neither alone does the same thing. The mustard adds a slight sharpness that keeps the sauce from tasting too sweet.
Serve on toast for breakfast or as a side with sausages and eggs. Also good as part of a jacket potato filling.

Add {{haricot-beans}} of drained haricot beans to the slow cooker. Add {{tinned-tomatoes}} of tinned tomatoes, {{tomato-puree}} of tomato puree, {{onion}} diced onion, and {{garlic}} of crushed garlic. Add {{dark-brown-sugar}} of dark brown sugar, {{worcestershire-sauce}} of Worcestershire sauce, {{english-mustard}} of English mustard, and {{sea-salt-fine}} of salt. Stir well to combine.
Set the slow cooker to LOW and cook for 6 to 8 hours. Stir once or twice during cooking if possible. The sauce should be thick and coating the beans. Taste before serving and adjust the seasoning.

rows.cause: The tinned tomatoes released more liquid than the beans absorbed.
rows.fix: Set to HIGH with the lid off for 30 minutes. Or stir in an extra tablespoon of tomato puree.

rows.symptom: The beans are too soft and mushy
rows.cause: Tinned beans cooked for 8 hours can become very soft and lose their shape.
rows.fix: Check at 6 hours next time and stop cooking when the beans are tender but still whole. The sauce improves with longer cooking even if the beans are done.

rows.cause: The balance of sugar and acidity depends on the tomatoes used.
rows.fix: Add a teaspoon of cider vinegar or red wine vinegar to balance. Taste again and adjust the mustard if needed.

rows.cause: The Worcestershire sauce or mustard amounts were too small, or the stock reduced and concentrated the salt too much.
rows.fix: Add another teaspoon of Worcestershire sauce and a pinch of smoked paprika. Stir well and leave on LOW for 30 more minutes.

content.text: Baked beans became a British breakfast staple through commercial tinned products from the early 1900s. Homemade versions have grown in popularity as people look for a less sweet, more savoury alternative. The slow cooker suits this recipe well because the long cook does what commercial canneries do: soften the beans slowly in the sauce until they are inseparable from it.
